summary.text: Lithium burns with a strongly red-tinged flame, and in pure oxygen the flame is even stronger.
summary.excerpt: Lithium burns with a strongly red-tinged flame if heated in air; in pure oxygen, the flame is more intense.

trigger.text: Lithium starts to burn when it is heated in air.
trigger.excerpt: Lithium burns with a strongly red-tinged flame if heated in air

hazard.text: Melted lithium catches fire quite easily and is then hard to put out.
hazard.excerpt: Molten lithium is quite easily ignited and is then difficult to extinguish.

hazard.text: Lithium oxide is corrosive and can injure the skin, the eyes and the breathing passages.
hazard.excerpt: A corrosive substance that can cause injury to the skin, eyes, and respiratory tract

whyNot.text: Gold is one of a few metals, along with silver and platinum, that do not react with oxygen.
whyNot.excerpt: However, gold, silver, and platinum do not react with oxygen.

whyNot.text: Oxygen mostly does not react with gold.
whyNot.excerpt: Oxygen is mostly unreactive with gold and platinum.

appearance.text: Lithium oxide is a white powder with no smell.

uses.text: Lithium oxide is used to soak up carbon dioxide gas.
uses.excerpt: Used as a carbon dioxide absorbent

uses.text: Lithium oxide is used to make special kinds of glass and ceramics.
uses.excerpt: to make specialty glasses and ceramics
